_comment: #3990 — the WHY-LAYER eval set. Frozen: tools/why_layer_rate.py pins this
file's sha256 and refuses to run against a different one (a changed eval set
is a NEW instrument, not a moved rate).
Every question's gold claim is OPERATOR-MEDIATED by construction: the
seeder creates a support point, the claim, and the operator between them
through the public write path (create_operator / mitigate_operator), so the
gold operator id is the id the product minted — W2 compares identity, never
text. `mitigation: null` and `operator_label: null` are MEASURED absences
(W1 must not invent a label, W3 must not fabricate a mitigation).
DECORRELATED BY DESIGN: `operator_label != null` and `mitigation != null`
are independent here (2 rows carry both, 2 label-only, 2 mitigation-only, 2
neither). A set where they always moved together could not attribute a W1
or a W3 failure to the right dimension.
KNOWN LIMITATION, stated rather than implied: every row is the same SHAPE
(one evidence -> one IMPL operator -> one claim). Mixed-edge claims (the
direct-IMPL leg) and claims mediated by more than one operator are outside
the set's reach; they are pinned by tests/test_why_operator_mediation.py
instead. This instrument measures the shipped shape, not every shape.
Abstention and verbatim grounding are NOT measured here — they belong to
tools/ask_shape_rate.py (L1/L3). Keeping them out means no question sits in
the denominator while being out of scope for the legs (no vacuous passes).

questions.question: Why do we believe the renewal completed in March?
questions.claim: the zephyrquill contract renewed in March
questions.support: billing ledger shows the zephyrquill renewal charge posted
questions.mitigation: the ledger was reconciled by hand once

questions.question: Why do we believe the seal is defective?
questions.claim: the obsidianlatch seal failed under load
questions.support: audit walked the obsidianlatch gasket after 40 cycles
questions.mitigation: the outage was a once-a-year event

questions.question: Why do we believe the vendor raised prices?
questions.claim: the harrowfen vendor raised unit prices in Q2
questions.support: the harrowfen invoice total rose 20 percent quarter over quarter

questions.question: Why do we believe the migration slipped?
questions.claim: the glintmarsh migration slipped a week
questions.support: staging burned half the glintmarsh window on a schema conflict

questions.question: Why do we believe the design was accepted?
questions.support: two reviewers signed off on the cinderhollow spec
questions.mitigation: one sign-off was conditional on a follow-up

questions.question: Why do we believe the cache is cold on boot?
questions.claim: the frostwhistle cache is cold on boot
questions.support: the frostwhistle boot trace shows zero cache hits for 40 seconds
questions.mitigation: the batch window was unusually small that night

questions.question: Why do we believe the retry budget is too small?
questions.claim: the emberquay retry budget is too small
questions.support: emberquay drained its retries in nine minutes during the outage

questions.question: Why do we believe the export path is unowned?
questions.claim: the sablewick export path has no owner
questions.support: the sablewick service map lists no on-call rotation for exports
